title: Probe and needle on the patient
view: Right groin and upper thigh from above, patient supine, seen from the foot of the bed: head at the top, lateral on the image left, medial on the right. Draped, with a window over the groin.
teachingPoint: Linear probe transverse-oblique just below and parallel to the inguinal ligament, over the AIIS then slid caudally to the iliopubic eminence, lateral to the femoral artery; needle in-plane from lateral to medial.
claims: Right groin from above, head at the top, lateral left, medial right - the same way round as the anatomy plate. Reuses the approved femoral block layout.
Purple: the ASIS, the AIIS (dashed, about 3 cm below the ASIS), the pubic tubercle and the inguinal ligament (dashed). Red dashes: the femoral artery's surface course.
Linear probe just below and parallel to the ligament, over the iliopubic eminence, lateral to the artery (record: transverse over the AIIS, slid caudally to the IPE; the vessels are medial).
Needle entering beyond the probe's lateral end, in line with it: in-plane from lateral to medial (record).
Labels: ASIS, AIIS, Inguinal ligament, Femoral artery.
